documentation.text:
Grants transient access to a handle for an account. This function does not do any
 checks and should be used with caution.
 This function is used in two scenarios:
   - For handles generated off-chain by the Handle Gateway, once the proof has been verified
   - For handles resulting from on-chain operations, where the caller naturally inherits
     rights on the output handle
 @param handle Handle identifier
 @param account Address of the account
Reverts if account lacks access to any handle in the array.

Checks if the handle is public, or if account has transient or persistent
 access to the handle.

addViewer(bytes32,address).details: Only an admin can add a viewer. The viewer address cannot be address(0).

params.viewer: The address to grant viewer role

allow(bytes32,address).details: Caller must have access (transient OR persistent) to the handle

params.account: The address to grant admin role

allowPublicDecryption(bytes32).details: The caller must be allowed to use the handle.      If not, the function reverts.

params.handle: Handle to mark as publicly decryptable.

allowTransient(bytes32,address).details: To grant transient access, the caller must already have permission on `handle`.      Transient access only lasts for the current transaction. It is the responsibility      of the application contract to convert this into persistent access via `allow()`      if needed.

returns.success: Bool handle indicating if the burn succeeded

returns.result: Bool handle indicating greater than or equal

returns._0: Whether the account can access the handle (persistent or transient).

burn(bytes32,bytes32,bytes32).notice: Computes a confidential burn operation. If the burn operation fails (e.g., due to underflow), the success handle will contain an encrypted `false` and the newBalanceFrom and newTotalSupply handles will contain the same values as the input balanceFrom and totalSupply handles.

disallowTransient(bytes32,address).notice: Revokes transient access to `handle` for address `account` within the current transaction.

div(bytes32,bytes32).notice: Performs a division between two encrypted values without safety checks. In the case of a division by zero, the result will be as follows:  - For unsigned integers uintN: encrypted MAX_UintN (i.e., 2^N - 1)  - For signed integers intN: encrypted MAX_IntN (i.e., 2^(N-1) - 1)

eq(bytes32,bytes32).notice: Checks equality between two encrypted values

ge(bytes32,bytes32).notice: Checks if left operand is greater than or equal to right operand

gt(bytes32,bytes32).notice: Checks if left operand is greater than right operand

isAllowed(bytes32,address).notice: Returns whether the account is allowed to use the `handle`, either due to allowTransient() or allow().

isPubliclyDecryptable(bytes32).notice: Checks whether a handle is publicly decryptable.

isViewer(bytes32,address).notice: Returns whether the account can view the handle.

le(bytes32,bytes32).notice: Checks if left operand is less than or equal to right operand

lt(bytes32,bytes32).notice: Checks if left operand is less than right operand

mint(bytes32,bytes32,bytes32).notice: Computes a confidential mint operation. If the minting operation fails (e.g., due to overflow), the success handle will contain an encrypted `false` and the newBalanceTo and newTotalSupply handles will contain the same values as the input balanceTo and totalSupply handles.

mul(bytes32,bytes32).notice: Performs a multiplication between two encrypted values without overflow check.

ne(bytes32,bytes32).notice: Checks inequality between two encrypted values

safeAdd(bytes32,bytes32).notice: Performs an addition between two encrypted values with overflow check. If the operation succeeds, the value of the success handle will be an encrypted `true` and the result handle's value will be the encrypted sum. If the operation fails (e.g., due to overflow), the success handle will contain an encrypted `false` and the result handle will contain an encrypted `0`.

safeDiv(bytes32,bytes32).notice: Performs a division between two encrypted values with division-by-zero check. If the operation succeeds, the value of the success handle will be an encrypted `true` and the result handle's value will be the encrypted quotient. If the operation fails (e.g., due to division by zero), the success handle will contain an encrypted `false` and the result handle will contain an encrypted `0`.

safeMul(bytes32,bytes32).notice: Performs a multiplication between two encrypted values with overflow check. If the operation succeeds, the value of the success handle will be an encrypted `true` and the result handle's value will be the encrypted product. If the operation fails (e.g., due to overflow), the success handle will contain an encrypted `false` and the result handle will contain an encrypted `0`.

safeSub(bytes32,bytes32).notice: Performs a subtraction between two encrypted values with underflow check. If the operation succeeds, the value of the success handle will be an encrypted `true` and the result handle's value will be the encrypted difference. If the operation fails (e.g., due to underflow), the success handle will contain an encrypted `false` and the result handle will contain an encrypted `0`.

select(bytes32,bytes32,bytes32).notice: Selects between two encrypted values based on a condition

setGateway(address).notice: Sets the gateway address in the contract's config.

setKmsPublicKey(bytes).notice: Sets the KMS public key used for ECIES encryption.

sub(bytes32,bytes32).notice: Performs a subtraction between two encrypted values without underflow check.

transfer(bytes32,bytes32,bytes32).notice: Computes a confidential transfer between two balances. The transfer will succeed if the sender has sufficient balance and fail otherwise. If the transfer fails, the success handle will contain an encrypted `false`, the newBalanceFrom and newBalanceTo handles will contain the same values as the input balanceFrom and balanceTo handles.

validateAllowedForAll(address,bytes32[]).notice: Checks whether the account is allowed to use all provided handles. Reverts with NotAllowed if any handle is not allowed.

validateDecryptionProof(bytes32,bytes).notice: Validates the decryption proof issued by the gateway for a given handle. The proof must be signed by the configured gateway. The proof uses a compact serialization: `signature (65 bytes) || decryptedResult (N bytes)`. The signature is placed first (fixed size) so that `decryptedResult` can be variable-length, supporting all current and future types that may exceed 32 bytes (e.g. encrypted strings).

validateInputProof(bytes32,address,bytes.notice: Validates that a handle provided by a user is:   - of expected type   - not expired   - issued for the correct app (caller)   - issued for the correct owner   - issued by the configured gateway (signed by the gateway wallet) or reverts otherwise. Handle format:  1 byte    4 bytes      1 byte  1 byte      25 bytes   [0]     [1------4]     [5]     [6]     [7-----------31] Version    ChainId       Type    Attrs      Pre-handle Proof format:  20 bytes       20 bytes        32 bytes            65 bytes [0-----19]    [20-----39]    [40--------71]    [72------------136]   Owner           App           CreatedAt       EIP-712 signature

wrapAsPublicHandle(bytes32,uint8).notice: Wraps a plaintext value into a deterministic public handle. The resulting handle has bit 0 of the attributes byte (byte 30) unset, meaning it can be non unique, it carries no ACL and is accessible by everyone. The same value and type always produce the same handle.

userdoc.notice: Access control for encrypted handles. Supports persistent and transient access, plus viewer and public-decryption roles.
